# LemonadeJS v6

Reactive micro-library. React-like patterns, ~5 KB gzip, zero dependencies, zero build step.
This file is the complete API. If something is not here, it does not exist.

## Setup

Zero-build (one file, one tag):
    <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lemonadejs@6/dist/lemonade.min.js"></script>
    <!-- global: lemonade.html, lemonade.mount, ... -->

Module:
    import { html, mount, type Component, type State } from 'lemonadejs';

## Components

A component is a plain function: (props, tools) => html`...`. No classes, no this, no hooks rules.

    import { html, mount, type Component } from 'lemonadejs';

    const Counter: Component<{ start?: number }> = (props, { state }) => {
        const count = state(props.start ?? 0);
        return html`<div>
            <p>${count}</p>
            <button onclick="${() => count.value++}">+1</button>
        </div>`;
    };

    mount(Counter, document.getElementById('app'));

## The four template rules (everything else follows from these)

1. ${state}            → live value; updates when the state changes
2. ${() => expr}       → live expression; re-runs when any state it READS changes
3. ${plainValue}       → one-time snapshot; plain strings are TEXT, never HTML (XSS-safe)
4. Loops/conditionals are just expressions returning html`...` views or arrays of them:
       ${() => items.value.map(x => html`<li>${x}</li>`)}
       ${() => valid.value && html`<div>shown when valid</div>`}
   Inside the inner template, plain snapshots (${x}) are correct: the outer arrow re-runs.

Slot values: string|number (text), false/true/null/undefined (nothing), html`` view, Node, array of these.

KEYS — when list items can REORDER, be inserted or removed, key the item's
root: matching becomes identity-based, the existing DOM (and any component
instances inside it, with their state) MOVES instead of rebuilding:

    ${() => rows.value.map(r => html`<tr key="${r.id}">...</tr>`)}
    key="${r}"            // the item object itself works (identity, Object.is)

key is a directive like bind/ref: consumed by the engine, never rendered,
never a component prop. Keys must be unique per list (duplicates warn
LJS-204 and rebuild). Lists that only append or change in place do not need
keys — the positional diff already reuses entries. Components in keyed
lists move WITH their state when item values are unchanged; an item whose
values changed rebuilds (pass stable references for props you do not want
to trigger that).

Trusted HTML (plain strings are ALWAYS escaped; this is the explicit opt-out):

    import { unsafe } from 'lemonadejs';
    html`<article>${unsafe(trustedHtmlFromCms)}</article>`   // never on user input

## State

    const count = state(0);                         // State<number>, inferred
    count.value++;                                  // assignment notifies automatically
    const s = state(0, (val, old) => {...});        // optional change callback

NOT React: state is NOT immutable. Two notification paths, one rule —
assignment notifies by itself; in-place mutation is allowed, free and SILENT
until you call touch():

    const rows = state(bigData);                    // 1M rows? fine
    rows.value[500].total = 9;                      // mutate in place — no copy, no proxy
    rows.touch();                                   // notify — DOM writes are delta-only
    rows.value = [...rows.value, newRow];           // assignment style also works (small data)

    import { batch } from 'lemonadejs';
    batch(() => {                                   // bulk ops: paste, sort, bulk delete
        for (const c of cells) rows.value[c.y][c.x] = c.v;
        rows.touch();                               // thousands of changes, ONE update pass
        selection.value = area;                     // bindings deduped across states
    });

The footgun (LJS-201): mutate without touch() and nothing updates.

Shared state (outside components, module scope):

    import { store } from 'lemonadejs';
    export const session = store({ user: null });   // any component can use ${session}
    export const theme = store('light', 'app-theme'); // persisted to localStorage

## Events and refs

    <button onclick="${() => save()}">         event = on* attribute + function (never strings; CSP-safe)
    <input onkeydown="${(e) => ...}" />        handler receives the DOM event
    <p ref="${(el) => { ... }}">               callback ref: receives the created element
    const box = ref<HTMLElement>();            object ref (useRef-style), import { ref }
    <p ref="${box}">                           box.current = the element; components: .current = the api
                                               .current is NULLED automatically when the DOM is disposed
Refs fire AFTER the nodes attach (same synchronous update, no waiting): the
element is connected, so focus() and getBoundingClientRect() work directly
inside a ref — no queueMicrotask/isConnected deferral is ever needed.

Annotate the ref parameter with the type you KNOW (you wrote the tag):
ref="${(el: HTMLInputElement) => el.focus()}" — no `as` casts. The engine
stays flexible (SVG and exotic elements accept any signature).

DOM listeners outside the template (document, window, another element) go
through the listen TOOL — never raw addEventListener in a component:

    const C: Component = (p, { listen }) => { ... };
    listen(document, 'mousemove', onMove);          // removed on unmount, automatically
    const off = listen(window, 'resize', onResize); // off() removes earlier (idempotent)

listen works anywhere — setup, onMount, or MID-GESTURE inside an event
handler: arm document mousemove/mouseup on mousedown, call off() on mouseup,
and a mid-drag unmount still cleans up. A forgotten removeEventListener is
not writable. (Listeners on the component's OWN elements stay in the
template: onclick="${...}".)

ONE RULE, NO EXCEPTIONS: all event and callback names are lowercase, HTML-style —
onclick, oninput, onchange, onsave, onitemclick (like the platform's onmousedown).
Any other casing warns LJS-305 in dev. On components, props are case-sensitive keys,
so onChange would be a DIFFERENT prop than onchange and silently ignored.

## Attributes

    <div class="btn ${active}">                mixed static + state → live string
    <input value="${name}" />                  form values set as properties (one-way)
    <input disabled />                         boolean attributes work
    checked="${boolState}"                     boolean property binding

## Styling

Dynamic styles — css() builds the style string from an object (typed keys,
automatic px on numbers, false/null entries skipped so conditionals compose):

    import { css } from 'lemonadejs';
    <div style="${() => css({ top: y.value, left: x.value, opacity: 0.5,
        background: active.value && 'red' })}">
    // → "top:12px;left:40px;opacity:0.5" — unitless props (opacity, z-index,
    // flex, line-height, order, font-weight, --custom) never get px

Component-owned CSS — a <style> tag inside html`` never enters the DOM tree:
its CSS is lifted at parse time and injected into document.head ONCE per
template, however many instances mount. A component ships working styling in
ONE file, in every deployment:

    const Chip: Component = () => html`<span class="lm-chip">
        <style>.lm-chip { padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 12px; }</style>
        ${props.label}
    </span>`;

Rules: the CSS must be static — ${...} inside <style> fails LJS-105 (styles
are parsed once; use style="" or CSS custom properties for per-instance
values). Styles are GLOBAL by design: prefix every selector with your
component class (lm-chip), exactly like the lm-<name>-* convention.

## Two-way binding

Native form elements — engine directive (consumed, never a DOM attribute):

    <input bind="${name}" />                   value ⇄ state (input event)
    <input type="checkbox" bind="${on}" />     checked ⇄ boolean state (change)
    <input type="radio" value="a" bind="${pick}" />   radio groups share one state
    <select bind="${choice}">...</select>      <textarea bind="${text}">

bind requires the STATE OBJECT (bind="${name}", never bind="name" or bind="${name.value}").
Only input/textarea/select. Do not combine bind with value/checked (LJS-304).

Components — bind is a plain prop, implemented with the bind() tool:

    import { html, type Component, type Bindable } from 'lemonadejs';

    const Switch: Component<Bindable<boolean>> = (props, { bind }) => {
        const checked = bind(props, false);   // external state if bound, local otherwise
        return html`<div class="${() => (checked.value ? 'on' : 'off')}"
            onclick="${() => checked.set(!checked.value)}"></div>`;
    };

    <${Switch} bind="${enabled}" onchange="${(v) => ...}" />   two-way
    <${Switch} />                                              standalone (local state)
    <${Switch} bind="${true}" />                               plain value = initial only

value.set(v) commits a component-initiated change: writes AND fires props.onchange.
Plain value.value = v writes silently (parent writes never echo onchange back).

## Component composition

Two equivalent ways to use a component:

    import { setComponents } from 'lemonadejs';
    setComponents({ Card, Modal });        // register once (typed, by value)...
    html`<Card title="x">...</Card>`     // ...then use by name anywhere (case-sensitive)

    html`<${Card} title="x" /></...>`    // or embed by value, no registration needed

Unknown/misspelled names raise LJS-104 at mount. Both forms take identical props.
Embedded by value:

    const Card: Component<{ title?: string; total?: State<number>; onsave?: (v: string) => void }> =
        (props) => html`<div class="card">
            <h3>${props.title}</h3>      <!-- literal attr → string snapshot -->
            <b>${props.total}</b>        <!-- state passed by reference → live -->
            ${props.children}            <!-- content between the tags -->
        </div>`;

    const App: Component = (props, { state }) => {
        const count = state(0);
        return html`<main>
            <${Card} title="Hello" total="${count}" onsave="${(v) => console.log(v)}">
                <p>children, bound to the PARENT scope: ${count}</p>
            </${Card}>
        </main>`;
    };

Props rules: literal attribute text → string; ${...} → passed by reference, untouched
(states stay live, callbacks callable, objects unstringified); `flag` alone → true.
Props are read-only (frozen in dev). Data flows up via callback props.

## Publishing components (contracts)

A plain function is a component. component(name, contract, fn) is for components that
become PRODUCTS — plugins, libraries, anything other frameworks or other agents consume.
The contract is the interface as a runtime artifact; everything derives from it.

    import { component, contract } from 'lemonadejs';

    export const Switch = component('switch', {
        bind: false,                 // bindable value — type and default inferred: boolean
        label: '',                   // prop: string, default ''
        count: 0,                    // prop: number — attribute "5" auto-coerced to 5
        data: Array,                 // constructor = type only, no default
        onchange: Function,          // event out
        api: { toggle: Function },   // imperative surface, exposed via props.ref
    }, (props, { bind }) => {
        const checked = bind(props, false);
        const toggle = () => checked.set(!checked.value);
        props.ref?.({ toggle });     // fulfill the declared api
        return html`<div class="${() => value.value ? 'on' : 'off'}"
            onclick="${toggle}">${props.label}</div>`;
    });

RULE: declared props arrive as LIVE STATES — props.label is State<string> in every
deployment, NON-OPTIONAL (the engine constructs every declared prop, so no ! and no
casts: props.max.value - props.min.value just typechecks). Declared on* events are
invocable as-is: props.onchange?.(value). Templates: ${props.label}. Logic:
props.label.value. Wrong types warn LJS-401 in dev; a prop the contract does NOT
declare warns LJS-402 with a did-you-mean suggestion; contract prop names must be
lowercase (they become HTML attributes). ApiOf<typeof Switch> names the api type a
ref receives — never hand-roll api shapes.

    contract(Switch)    // → { name, props: {label: {type,default}}, bind, events, api }
                        // the schema an agent reads INSTEAD of the source

    createWebComponent(Switch)   // <lm-switch>, zero options, ALL derived:
                                 // live attributes (coerced), element properties
                                 // (el.label = 'x'), bind as el.value, declared
                                 // events dispatched as real CustomEvents

    import { verify } from 'lemonadejs/test';
    verify(Switch)      // → { pass, checks } — conformance against the contract:
                        // mounts, every prop (plain + live state), events, bind,
                        // api actually exposed. Generate a component and its
                        // proof in one breath.

Sugar — singleton component services (replaces external state tools like Redux):

    <${Notifications} expose />              // instance publishes its DECLARED api on mount
    use(Notifications)?.notify('saved')      // anywhere; typed by the import; null until mounted
    // only api: {...} crosses the boundary — internals stay closed over, unreachable
    // singletons: register once, never touch; re-exposing warns LJS-501 (last wins);
    // unmount withdraws. For app-owned logic prefer store() + exported actions.

Interop with other reactive worlds (React, Svelte, Rx) — subscribe + peek:

    const value = useSyncExternalStore(rows.subscribe, rows.peek);   // React reads
    useEffect(() => { rows.value = props.data; }, [props.data]);     // React writes

subscribe(cb) has addEventListener semantics: cb runs UNTRACKED, pinned to that
one state — reads inside it never create dependencies, so read-modify-write
(count.value++) and reading other states are both safe.

Derived values: computed (a tool) — the fix for "captured once" snapshots:

    const C: Component = (props, { state, computed }) => {
        const qty = state(2);
        const total = computed(() => qty.value * (props.price?.value ?? 0));  // stays LIVE
        return html`<b>${total}</b>`;   // re-renders when qty OR props.price change
    };
    // write the sources, never the computed; disposed with the component

Renderer-caused focus events: removing a focused element (branch swap, unmount)
fires focusout exactly like a user leaving. Anything that closes/commits on
focusout must check:

    import { isDisposing } from 'lemonadejs';
    onfocusout="${(e) => { if (isDisposing()) return; close(); }}"

## Lifecycle

    const C: Component = (props, { state, onMount, onUnmount, listen, unmount }) => {
        onMount((el) => {
            const id = setInterval(tick, 1000);
            return () => clearInterval(id);     // cleanup, runs on unmount
        });
        listen(document, 'keydown', onKey);     // removed on unmount automatically
        onUnmount(() => {...});
        return html`<div></div>`;
    };

    const handle = mount(C, root);  // { el, unmount() }
    handle.unmount();               // removes DOM, disposes everything

## Web components (interop with other stacks)

    import { createWebComponent } from 'lemonadejs';
    createWebComponent('switch', Switch);          // defines <lm-switch> for any HTML/framework
    createWebComponent('card', Card, { prefix: 'app' });   // <app-card>
    // attributes at connect time arrive as string props; el.props = {...} for rich values
    // for composition INSIDE lemonade, use <Card /> or <${Card} /> instead

## Forms (lemonadejs/forms)

    import { form } from 'lemonadejs/forms';
    const f = form({ name: '', address: { city: '' } });   // states mirroring the shape
    html`<input bind="${f.name}" /><input bind="${f.address.city}" />`
    f.$get()                        // plain data object, nested
    f.$set({ name: 'Ana' })         // partial updates, nested supported

## Verify your own output (lemonadejs/test)

    import { render } from 'lemonadejs/test';     // needs a DOM (browser or jsdom)

    const t = render(Counter, { start: 5 });
    t.query('button')!.click();                 // querySelector, scoped
    t.query('p')!.textContent === '6';          // assert
    t.queryAll('li');                           // array of elements
    t.text();                                   // full visible text
    t.snapshot();                               // deterministic indented DOM tree (diffable)
    t.inspect();                                // { component, states: [...], children } JSON
    t.unmount();

    import { flush, setRect } from 'lemonadejs/test';
    await flush();                              // drain microtasks + zero-delay timers
    setRect(el, { left: 10, width: 200, height: 24 });  // geometry in jsdom (no layout
                                                // there) — modal/tooltip/drag become testable

## Debugging

    import { inspect, explain, setComponents } from 'lemonadejs';
    inspect(element)        // live component tree for any element: names, state values, children
    explain('LJS-202')      // long-form doc for any error code, offline

Dev vs production is decided by the BUILD you load, not a runtime flag:
dist/lemonade.dev.js (script tag) and the bundler "development" condition give
warnings + checks; dist/lemonade.min.js and production bundles have all dev
code eliminated — production pays zero.

## Error codes (stable, pattern-matchable)

    LJS-001 component is not a function          LJS-201 mutation is silent — touch() or assign
    LJS-002 must return html`...`              LJS-202 slot is a snapshot — wrap: ${() => ...}
    LJS-003 mount root must be an element        LJS-203 update loop — don't assign states in expressions
    LJS-101 mismatched closing tag               LJS-301 events need functions, not strings
    LJS-102 unclosed tag                         LJS-302 bind needs a state: bind="${state}"
    LJS-104 unknown component — setComponents    LJS-303 bind: input/textarea/select only
    LJS-105 ${} not allowed in that position     LJS-204 duplicate key in a list — keys are unique
                                                 LJS-304 bind owns value — drop the value attribute
    LJS-401 prop violates its contract           LJS-305 callbacks are lowercase: onclick, onsave
    LJS-402 unknown prop (did-you-mean hint)     LJS-501 expose once — singletons, never touch

## Migrating from v5

    v5                                   v6
    return render => render`...`         return html`...` (tag renamed, no wrapper)
    lemonade.render(Comp, root)          mount(Comp, root)
    this.prop / {{self.prop}}            const prop = state(...) + ${prop}
    onload(fn) / :ready                  onMount(fn) (return a cleanup fn) / ref="${fn}"
    self.onchange(prop, o, n)            state(v, (val, old) => ...) per state
    :loop="self.rows"                    ${() => rows.value.map(r => html`...`)}
    :render="${cond}"                    ${() => cond.value && html`...`}
    :bind="self.name"                    bind="${name}" (elements) / bind() tool (components)
    lemonade.set/get/dispatch (Sugar)    store() + exported action functions in a module
    lemonade.set(k, fn, true) persist    store(initial, 'storage-key')
    setComponents({ Card }) + <Card/>    same — or embed by value: <${Card} />
    lm-path / setPath forms              form() from lemonadejs/forms ($get/$set)
    HTML strings in slots                escaped by default; unsafe(html) for trusted markup
    self.refresh('prop') / refresh()     state.touch() after in-place mutation; assignment otherwise

## Common mistakes

WRONG  ${valid.value && html`...`}            evaluates once — frozen (LJS-202 warns)
RIGHT  ${() => valid.value && html`...`}

WRONG  items.value.push(x)  alone               silent (LJS-201) — nothing updates
RIGHT  items.value.push(x); items.touch()       — or items.value = [...items.value, x]

WRONG  <Card title="x" />  without registering  LJS-104 — register first: setComponents({ Card })
RIGHT  setComponents({ Card }) then <Card />, or <${Card} title="x" /> with no registration

WRONG  onclick="doSomething()"                  LJS-301 — string handlers don't exist
RIGHT  onclick="${() => doSomething()}"

WRONG  <input bind="${name.value}" />           LJS-302 — that's a snapshot, not a state
RIGHT  <input bind="${name}" />

WRONG  onChange="${fn}" / onSave="${fn}"        LJS-305 — all callbacks are lowercase
RIGHT  onchange="${fn}" / onsave="${fn}"
